contexts.description: Internal admin surface (Velín mission control): monitors data-ingestion loop progress, tripwire alerts, vault heads, and the review hub. The loops sub-module reads and drives loop state from JSON drive-log files, enabling an operator to watch and intervene in running ingestion jobs.
contexts.name: admin-control

contexts.description: App chrome: left nav rail, mobile nav, and sidebar wired to the navModel that declares modules and per-page section anchors. Controls which routes opt out of the shell and tracks the active section for scroll-synced highlighting.
contexts.name: app-shell

contexts.description: Provides the global Next.js app shell (root layout, error boundaries, metadata, robots/sitemap, global CSS tokens) plus the admin control panel used by maintainers to inspect ingestion loops and manage access gates. The admin surface uses server actions (gateActions, loopActions) and a JSON API route for loop state. Static legal/privacy pages and the archived Rentgen art-direction page are also housed here as leaf pages with no loader dependencies.
contexts.name: app-shell-admin

contexts.description: BudgetMirror surface for 132 Czech municipalities: MONITOR time-series data, peer-group comparison, and supplier-trail tracing from municipal contracts to beneficiaries. Generated data snapshots for budget and supplier tables sit beside the derivation logic.
contexts.name: budget-mirror

contexts.description: Core shared infrastructure for all case loops. Provides the canonical batch apply/persist pipeline (apply-batch, persist-batch), a citation backfill utility, a deterministic ordering comparator used by money and law loops, and Kiosek source adapters that build, slice, and validate KIOS payloads before submission.
contexts.name: case-loops-core

contexts.description: Component-library conformance checker ported from the personas repo. Runs the golden-path census engine against configured rules to verify UI primitives adhere to the shared design system contract. Includes the rule engine, library index, fixture trees for testing, and a check-library-adherence script that detects local drift from the upstream census engine.
contexts.name: census-quality

contexts.api_surface: GET /atlas/atlas.json, GET /data/manifest.json, GET /data/snapshot.json, GET /denik/feed.json, GET /denik/feed.xml, GET /schranka/feed.json, GET /schranka/feed.xml, GET /schranka/novinky.json
contexts.description: Provides the public data-transparency surfaces: the Atlas data-quality scorecard (/atlas with a JSON API), the data-releases page (/data with manifest and snapshot feeds), the Deník chronological record (/denik with JSON/XML feeds), and the Schránka follow-list with delta feeds (/schranka). These routes expose machine-readable JSON and RSS/XML feeds alongside human-readable pages, making the platform's data layer inspectable and subscribable by external consumers.
contexts.name: civic-feed-data

contexts.api_surface: composite(), getVerdict(), analyseKgMoney() — consumed by /zebricek and /poslanec loaders
contexts.description: The CivicScore computation engine: contribution formula (pillars → composite), legacy and trend variants, score-citation sourcing, legibility checks, low-score reason extraction, workhorse flavour labels, and knowledge-graph verdict/money analysis. This is the analytical heart of the platform — every MP's rank derives from here. The colocated tests enforce that `score === composite(pillars)` at all times.
contexts.name: civic-score-engine

contexts.description: Score composition, duel mechanics, and provenance layer for CivicScore: derives component fills from raw graph data, resolves claims with provenance receipts, and drives the head-to-head Souboj comparison flow with URL-serializable parameters.
contexts.name: civicscore-duel-scoring

contexts.description: CivicScore leaderboard surface showing all 207 MPs ranked by composite civic score with region (kraj) filtering, reader lens weighting, and search. Includes the Metodika pages that expose the formula and the regional breakdown picker.
contexts.name: civicscore-leaderboard

contexts.description: Shared library for parsing Czech parliamentary open-data formats: escape-aware UNL (Informix UNLOAD) parsing, fatal windows-1250 decoding, a dependency-free capped ZIP reader, and Czech ASCII folding. Provides the canonical normalization layer consumed by ingest adapters throughout `lib/ingest/`. All three parsers ship with colocated vitest tests.
contexts.name: czech-civic-data

contexts.description: Velín instrument panel's feed lane: dated-fact rows, exhibit snapshots, and the public-wire feed that surfaces recent graph activity to readers. Handles feed relevance scoring, freshness gates, and the mock fallback panel.
contexts.name: dashboard-feed

contexts.description: Velín's state-graph slice: renders the knowledge-graph canvas with node/edge traversal, chamber composition chart, and the leaderboard ledger. Drives the DashboardPage orchestrator and its graph selection state.
contexts.name: dashboard-graph

contexts.api_surface: getAtlasScore(), checkTripwires(), isPlausibleDate() — consumed by /atlas loader and cross-cutting guards
contexts.description: Data-quality and coverage analysis: atlas source scoring, overall quality metrics, language-gate classification for copy safety, tripwire invariant checks, and plausible-date boundary validation. These modules power the /atlas source-quality scorecard and the cross-cutting reliability guards that prevent implausible dates or language violations from reaching the reader.
contexts.name: data-quality-analysis

contexts.description: Data release train and per-source quality scorecard: /data lists published dataset snapshots with feed address books; /atlas shows per-source data-quality ratings, unrated sources are never silently treated as zero. Together they form the reader-facing transparency layer over the ingestion pipeline.
contexts.name: data-releases-atlas

contexts.api_surface: Internal engine APIs: open(), storeCopy, maintenance scheduler — not consumed directly by features
contexts.description: PGlite engine internals: DDL declaration, durability contract, WAL maintenance scheduler, store copy utility, pre-migration snapshot safety, accounting/ledger, and the open-retry guard. Together these make the embedded Postgres reliable across process restarts and safe to migrate. The durability contract and maintenance scheduler are especially critical — they document why fsync is off and when checkpoints fire.
contexts.name: db-pglite-engine

contexts.api_surface: Typed repository methods: upsertNode, upsertEdge, getVotes, getWeights — consumed by loaders and analysis pipelines
contexts.description: All PGlite repository implementations: knowledge-graph CRUD (kg, graph, kg-bitemporal), votes, vote-tags, scoring weights, ledger, review queue, provenance, change log, and analysis results. These are the typed data-access objects that translate between the SQL schema and the domain types consumed by analysis and feature loaders. Truncation guards and bitemporal tests cover correctness invariants.
contexts.name: db-repositories

contexts.api_surface: getStore(), storeReady(), loaderGuard — server-only; consumed by feature loaders
contexts.description: Top-level database store API: exposes `getStore()`, `storeReady()`, the PGlite store singleton, readiness lifecycle, read-cap enforcement, and the sole SQL migration. This is the server-only boundary that all feature loaders cross to reach the embedded Postgres. Depends on the PGlite engine below it and is consumed by every `get*Data.ts` loader across features.
contexts.name: db-store-api

contexts.description: Deník republiky chronological record: derives the dated civic feed from the knowledge graph, encodes it as RSS/JSON feeds, and enforces feed length limits. Handles Prague-timezone day boundaries for accurate dated grouping.
contexts.name: denik-feed

contexts.description: Dukazy evidence chain surface: derives a typed evidence feed from review-audit records, encodes and limits feed entries, and presents the review audit trail for analyst-approved claims. Bridges raw graph nodes with reader-facing evidence packets.
contexts.name: dukazy-evidence

contexts.description: CivicScore effort-scoring case-loop scripts, both active and archived. These scripts extract and score parliamentary effort inputs (role windows, tenure, dossiers, rapporteur loads), gate proposed prop payloads against the graph copy, and produce the scored ledger that feeds the CivicScore computation. Archive contains superseded pass42 and batch 8-10 scripts.
contexts.name: effort-case-loops

contexts.description: Publishable ESLint flat-config plugin that encodes the project's civic-transparency doctrine as nine machine-enforced rules: no silent failures, server/client import boundary, a11y (role-button keydown, reduced-motion fallback), design-token color discipline, number provenance (no raw display, require SourceNote citation), and SourceNote size-override prevention. The plugin is registered in `eslint.config.mjs` under the `custom/` prefix and is the authoritative implementation — `eslint-rules/*.cjs` in the app root are one-line shims pointing here.
contexts.name: eslint-plugin-civic-transparency-rules

contexts.description: Tests and reference documentation for every rule in the `eslint-plugin-civic-transparency` package. Each test module uses ESLint's `RuleTester` with valid/invalid cases drawn from the rules' own decision logic; `run-all.mjs` is the test harness entry point exercised by `npm run test:rules`. The `docs/rules/` folder provides a human-readable explanation of each rule's rationale, options, and fix guidance.
contexts.name: eslint-plugin-civic-transparency-tests

contexts.description: Compatibility shim layer that re-exports the nine civic-transparency ESLint rules from their canonical home in `packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/` so historical file paths and documented commands remain functional. Each `.cjs` file is a one-line `module.exports = require(...)` forwarder; the two test files in `__tests__/` forward to the moved RuleTester suites and also assert shim equivalence so a drifted shim fails CI. Depended on by `eslint.config.mjs` via the `custom` rule-prefix registration.
contexts.name: eslint-rule-shims

contexts.description: Graph permalink and forensic-view layer: generates citation permalink cards with OG images, exposes a forensic fact-view over graph edges, and formats structured facts for the cite-view component. Permalink staleness is surfaced above the content.
contexts.name: graph-analysis

contexts.description: Interactive knowledge-graph canvas: renders the whole-graph playground with pan/zoom view transforms, node culling for performance, trail path computation, and kind-based visual styling. Owns the viewport and drives node selection state.
contexts.name: graph-canvas

contexts.description: Routes for the knowledge-graph canvas (/graf) and citation permalink cards (/graf/p/[ref] with OG image and bundle API), the Civic Claim Gate for re-deriving pasted citations (/overeni), source-reference permalinks (/zdroj/[ref]), the evidence register (/dukazy with JSON/XML feeds), and the testimony surface (/svedectvi). Together these surfaces expose graph provenance, let readers verify claims against the live record, and provide shareable evidence permalinks with OpenGraph previews.
contexts.name: graph-evidence-provenance

contexts.description: Self-contained Claude Code CLI benchmark harness measuring model quality and cost across aggregation, join, predicate, and semantic operations. Uses a cascade strategy that switches models mid-run (Haiku → Sonnet → Opus) based on difficulty. Runs standalone via tsx with no app imports, using OAuth subscription credentials.
contexts.name: hybrid-benchmark

contexts.description: Database maintenance, dev tooling, and smoke-test scripts. Covers PGlite backup/restore/migrate/accounting operations, a self-contained DuckDB/SQLite benchmarking suite (db-bench), the live-graph sentinel that asserts data invariants on a read-only copy, doc-sync checks, the pre-push copy-check hook, and the migration generator.
contexts.name: infrastructure-scripts

contexts.api_surface: emitChangeEvent(), parsedText() — consumed by all source adapters
contexts.description: Core ingest utilities: change-event emission, normalisation helpers, PDF text caching (stamped sidecar to avoid re-parse), URL-list parsing, and zip extraction. These are the shared primitives that every source adapter calls when fetching and pre-processing raw data before it reaches the knowledge graph. parsedText.ts is the key cost-avoidance layer for PDF-heavy sources.
contexts.name: ingest-core

contexts.api_surface: fetchPspActivity(), fetchSmlouvy(), fetchIsvz(), fetchMonitor() — called by da:* pipeline scripts
contexts.description: Source adapters for every Czech open-data endpoint: PSP parliamentary data (activity + legislation), ISVZ public procurement register, Smlouvy.gov contracts (live API + bulk dump), MONITOR municipal budget series, Kiosek PDF disclosures, Volby election results, and a generic pumper/backoff utility. Each adapter fetches, parses, and normalises its source into typed ingest payloads that the knowledge-graph pipeline consumes.
contexts.name: ingest-sources

contexts.description: Deterministic knowledge-graph computation and promotion pipeline. Reads raw civic data from PGlite (kg_node/kg_edge tables), computes weighted edges (co-vote agreement, rebellion rates, committee influence), and promotes gated LLM-verified verdicts into the graph. Entry points are kg-compute.ts for the deterministic pass and kg-promote.ts for the verdict promotion pass; kg-props-check, kg-repair-orphans, and slice-stats are maintenance utilities.
contexts.name: kg-pipeline

contexts.api_surface: getGlyph(), computeLayout(), propRegistry — consumed by /graf feature and MP profile graph panels
contexts.description: Knowledge-graph rendering primitives: glyph definitions (node visual type → icon/colour), force-directed layout engine, property registry (the canonical prop-registry.json schema), and source-link resolution. These are consumed by the /graf canvas and by any surface that renders a graph node visually. The prop-registry drives both ingest and display, making it the schema contract between the two.
contexts.name: kg-primitives

contexts.description: Archived Rentgen art direction (noindex lab): a terminal-style UI variant rendered against the same knowledge graph data, preserved as a living reference for alternative design directions. Not linked from the app shell.
contexts.name: labs-rentgen

contexts.description: Covers the public entry points: the Konstrukt landing page, the Velín instrument-panel dashboard (including exponat detail drilldowns), the CivicScore leaderboard and methodology page, the Kompas political-compass surface, the plakát print view, and the embedded leaderboard widget. These thin route files mount feature components from features/landing, features/dashboard, features/civicscore, and features/volby, and set per-route metadata. The embed route serves the leaderboard as a standalone embeddable page.
contexts.name: landing-dashboard-civicscore

contexts.description: Konstrukt-design landing surface that presents the hero ranking, hemicycle seat chart, leaderboard specimen, and module navigation to first-time visitors. Renders from real leaderboard loader data with labelled mock fallback. Depends on civicscore leaderboard loader and shared primitive catalog.
contexts.name: landing-page

contexts.description: Referendum sub-feature under the landing surface: collects public responses to policy questions and aggregates real-time vote tallies with OG image generation for share cards. Isolated sub-route backed by its own server loader and a stamped embed codec.
contexts.name: landing-referendum

contexts.description: Historical archive of superseded law case-loop scripts from completed analysis passes. Each file is a numbered batch script (e.g. prepare-batch-011.ts, collision-check-005.ts) that was retired after its pass completed or its logic was absorbed into the current active scripts. Kept for replay and audit; never re-run.
contexts.name: law-case-archive

contexts.description: LawWatch legislative analysis case-loop scripts. These scripts drive the batch process of analysing Czech bills and laws for collisions, sector attribution, amendment tracking, and verdict gating against the knowledge graph. The loop reads from PGlite copies, produces JSON payloads for LLM verification batches, and promotes gated results back via kg-promote.
contexts.name: law-case-loops

contexts.description: LawWatch deep-analysis layer: statute dossier pages, dependency radar, forensic index, sector attribution derivation, and statute-reference codec. Drives the bill and statute detail routes and the radar ledger visualization.
contexts.name: lawwatch-analysis

contexts.description: LawWatch main surface and bill browser: lists 141 bills and 101 enacted laws with their forensic register, surfaces statute collisions, and exposes sector attribution claims as a public wire. Powers the /zakony route and the Collisions sub-page.
contexts.name: lawwatch-watch

contexts.description: Historical archive of superseded FollowTheMoney case-loop scripts from completed analysis passes. Includes earlier batch validation scripts, stale ICO resolution utilities, and triage scripts from batches 9-14 that have been superseded by the current active scripts.
contexts.name: money-case-archive

contexts.description: MP and company case-file sub-routes under FollowTheMoney: renders dossiers of financial ties per MP and per company, resolves ownership chains, and assembles evidence packets. Derives lead-dossier targets from graph traversal.
contexts.name: money-case-files

contexts.description: FollowTheMoney financial-transparency analysis scripts. These scripts sweep ownership chains, harvest public-contract data from ARES/VR, resolve ICO nodes, detect indirect ownership exposures, and triage company-to-politician ties. They write structured payloads for LLM verification and promote gated verdicts back into the knowledge graph.
contexts.name: money-case-loops

contexts.description: FollowTheMoney main surface: tie ledger, money graph visualization, and core data layer. Derives reachable money flows through the knowledge graph, classifies tie strength, and exposes a public wire of recent financial connections.
contexts.name: money-core

contexts.description: Verification console, review queue, and conflict-of-interest (střety) detection for FollowTheMoney. Surfaces analyst review actions, derives procurement–vote collisions for MPs who voted on statutes relevant to their business ties, and provides the component palette for the money surfaces.
contexts.name: money-review-conflicts

contexts.description: The MP case-file surface (Spis): renders score breakdown, work dossier, money ties, rebellion record, career spine, and absence log for each of the 207 MPs. Derives rebellion provenance and career spine from the knowledge graph and falls back to labelled mock data.
contexts.name: mp-profile

contexts.api_surface: getContextProvider(), getMoneyFeed(), getLawVerdict() — consumed by /poslanec loader
contexts.description: MP case-file analysis: context model and provider (the six score-component slots), public-body resolution, copy generation for public descriptions, committee-claim extraction, rapporteur load computation, tenure copy, money-feed shaping, and law-verdict derivation. These modules feed the /poslanec spis (case file) surface with structured, source-cited facts about an individual MP.
contexts.name: mp-profile-analysis

contexts.description: Thin route layer for three interconnected accountability modules: the MP case-file profile (/poslanec/[id]), the FollowTheMoney money-flow surfaces (/penize and its sub-routes for individual MPs, firms, kauzy, kontrola, and střety), and the BudgetMirror municipal budget pages (/rozpocty). Each route mounts the corresponding feature component and delegates all data loading to server-only loaders. The penize routes cover conflict-of-interest detection, company tie ledgers, and MP financial packages.
contexts.name: mp-profiles-money-budget

contexts.description: Civic Claim Gate: lets readers paste a cited claim and re-derives it against today's knowledge graph, returning a typed verdict with provenance. Maintains a guide of example claims, detects reference patterns, and exposes live figures for round-trip verification.
contexts.name: overeni-claim-gate

contexts.description: Schranka accountless follow list: stores watched entity keys in localStorage, computes server-side deltas against the latest graph state, and exposes a personalized news feed without requiring user accounts. Telemetry is scrubbed of PII before any emission.
contexts.name: schranka-follow-list

contexts.api_surface: checkAdminGate(), issueToken(), verifyToken() — consumed by admin route handlers
contexts.description: Security primitives: admin-gate access control (guards admin routes against unauthorised access) and token generation/verification utilities. These are consumed by the admin-facing routes and any surface that issues or validates short-lived tokens. Isolated leaf directory — small by design, high correctness bar.
contexts.name: security-gates

contexts.api_surface: formatCzech(), claimRegistry, CitableNumber — consumed by all feature surfaces
contexts.description: Cross-cutting shared primitives: labelled mock/sample domain data (lib/civic), the claim registry and CitableNumber component that power source-citation enforcement, Czech number formatting (lib/format.ts), analytics event emission (lib/analytics.ts), and i18n configuration. These modules are imported everywhere — format.ts and CitableNumber are lint-enforced brand requirements for every rendered number.
contexts.name: shared-data

contexts.description: Domain-agnostic primitive catalog used across all feature surfaces. Contains SourceNote (provenance citation), StatTile, DataUnavailable, Combobox, AnimatedScore, and other lint-enforced reusable widgets that must receive all data via props and never import from features/*.
contexts.name: shared-primitives

contexts.description: Cross-feature provenance receipt system, forensic overlay mode, and poster/share frame. ProvenanceCapsule and ReceiptPage let readers follow any cited figure back to its source node; ForensicProvider toggles annotated overlays; PosterFrame wraps any surface for shareable export.
contexts.name: shared-provenance-forensic

contexts.description: Top-level app shell components used across all routes. LanguageSwitcher toggles the CS/EN locale by flipping the NEXT_LOCALE cookie via a server action and refreshing the RSC tree in place. MpProfileBeacon is a zero-render analytics beacon that fires a Plausible 'mp-profile-view' event on MP profile mounts, delegating to lib/analytics.ts which silently no-ops without NEXT_PUBLIC_PLAUSIBLE_DOMAIN.
contexts.name: shell-ui-components

contexts.description: Public procurement (Věstník veřejných zakázek) case-loop scripts. These scripts load monthly tender feeds, compute competition flags, detect monopolistic supplier patterns, build batch LLM payloads for deep reads, and persist enriched procurement records back into the knowledge graph.
contexts.name: tender-case-loops

contexts.api_surface: createPgliteFixture(), testLanes — consumed by all integration and unit tests
contexts.description: Test-support infrastructure: PGlite fixture/template factories for integration tests, lane-partitioned vitest sequencer, flake-detection registry with per-test history tracking, sentinel invariant checker, server-boundary assertion, gate-ladder progression tests, and a crash-writer utility. These modules make the test suite reliable and parallelisable — the flake registry and sentinel are especially important for catching regressions before they land.
contexts.name: test-infrastructure

contexts.api_surface: getElectionRules(), getContestedSeats() — consumed by /volby feature loader
contexts.description: Election analysis logic: contested-seat detection, regional (kraj) result shaping, election-term boundary rules, and shared election types. These modules underpin the /volby surface — given a voter's municipality, they determine which ballot subjects apply, which seats are contested, and which election cycle is active. Isolated leaf directory with no intra-lib imports beyond shared types.
contexts.name: volby-analysis

contexts.description: Volby election mirror: the flagship voter surface with municipality/region/list lookup, ballot-keyed subject cards, a severity ledger of procurement and conflict findings, and a dated outcome timeline. Derives findings at read time from the knowledge graph per electoral jurisdiction.
contexts.name: volby-elections

contexts.description: VoteTrack chamber view: vote ledger, hemicycle seat chart, discipline board, and seismograph for the full 207-MP chamber. Reads themed vote batches from the graph, reconciles the chamber self-count, and applies silver-layer aggregation for display.
contexts.name: votetrack-chamber

contexts.description: Political compass (Kompas) and vote-record derivation layer: lets readers answer policy questions and matches their positions against every MP's roll-call history. The record sub-module reconciles raw vote rows against club thresholds and derives typed vote outcomes.
contexts.name: votetrack-kompas-record

contexts.description: Route layer for VoteTrack (/hlasovani), LawWatch (/zakony with per-law detail, predpis lookup, and kolize collision feed), the Volby voter-mirror surface (/volby with obec/kraj/snemovna sub-routes), regional views (/kraj), and the referendum surface. These pages mount the corresponding feature components and wire law-collision and vote feeds as JSON/XML API routes. The volby surface is the flagship voter lookup: ballot-keyed subjects and a severity ledger composed at read time.
contexts.name: voting-legislation-elections
